title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #3580 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3580: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 42716908774](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42716908774) on `bot/issue-3496` (`e557876`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [rust (test server api)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42716908774/job/129503906615) | 7m 24s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42727191254)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`rust (test server api)` ran 7m 24s in CI run 42716908774, tripping the 7-minute alert (#73). Split it so every resulting job finishes under the 5-minute target with headroom. The bot-alone tool is a shard count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): raise `"server api"` from 1 to 4, so each of the four jobs runs the ~300 tests whose names hash to it. A person then updates the bot's pin test that any count change breaks (precedent #3280), and only if the pull request's CI still shows a shard at or over 5 minutes, splits the group in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change | `[rust-test]` `"server api" = 1` becomes `= 4`, plus a comment line in the file's existing style naming the 7m 24s and #3580 |
| `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` | change by a person | `JOBS` gains the four shard names; the `{(1, 1)}` shards assertion gains the four shard tuples (exact lines in Open questions) |
| `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` | change by a person, conditional | Split the `server api` group into lib-only and integration-only groups (exact TOML in Open questions), only if the new shards still miss 5 minutes |

Must not touch: `.github/` (bot), `bot/` (bot), `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `crates/`, `apps/`, `e2e/`, `spec/` (no game rule is involved, so no spec section or ruling governs this; the governing docs are the `ci.yml` header's five-minute budget, `ci-duration.yml`'s TARGET 5 / ALERT 7, and the `scripts/ci-shards.toml` / `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` / `matrix.py` design from #3072). Do not change other counts, `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs` `WEIGHTS`, `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, and do not move any test to daily (no single slow test was found, and the pull request must keep its coverage).

## Steps

1. Re-read `scripts/ci-shards.toml` lines 15-29 (the `[rust-test]` table and the comment explaining why a count never skips a test) and `.github/ci/matrix.py` `shard()` (CRC-32 of the test name decides its shard, so every test lands in exactly one shard for any count).
2. In `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, replace the line `"server api" = 1` with the following, keeping every other line byte-identical:
   ```toml
   # `server api` ran 7m 24s (#3580): about 1,200 tests (every tests/api module but
   # practice, plus the lib's api:: tests). 4 shards of about 300 tests each, so each
   # shard should finish under five minutes with headroom; each shard recompiles the
   # group's binaries again, as above.
   "server api" = 4
   ```
   Why 4, decided here since the builder cannot see CI times: 444 s total is compile (repeats per shard, likely 200-260 s given the engine and cards take about two minutes per job per the `rust-test.toml` header plus the server lib and two test binaries) plus run (splits three or four ways, ~1,200 fast fake-store API tests). A count of 2 likely still lands over 5 minutes; 3 is borderline; 4 lands around 260-290 s in the likely splits. Rejected: 2 (no headroom), 8 (more runners for almost no gain, since compile repeats), and a new group first (needs `.github/`, which the bot may not change, and a lib/integration split barely cuts compile since both build the server lib).
3. Verify the matrix locally with `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix > /tmp/matrix-3580.out 2> /tmp/matrix-3580.err`, then `grep "rust (test server api" /tmp/matrix-3580.err`. Expect exactly four lines: `rust (test server api 1/4)` through `rust (test server api 4/4)`, and no other new job name. A count must be a whole number 1-8 and the name must match a group, or the `changes` job fails; 4 satisfies both.
4. Run `cd bot && python3 -m unittest test_ci_matrix -v`. Expect every test to pass except `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs`, which must fail on the `JOBS` list and the `{(1, 1)}` assertion. That single failure is the person's follow-up in Open questions, not a defect: do not edit `bot/` to green it, do not skip or ignore it, and do not touch any other file.
5. Run `git status --porcelain`. Expect only `M scripts/ci-shards.toml`. No Rust, catalog, patch, ruling, web, or e2e file may change, so no cargo test, typecheck, or spec check is needed from the builder; the harness re-runs its checks after.

## Tests

- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` (stdout/stderr as in step 3): asserts the four `server api k/4` jobs exist with the group's unchanged `test` filters, scope `server`, and cache `server`. Shard 1 alone carries the binaries check; the group has no doc tests.
- `cd bot && python3 -m unittest test_ci_matrix -v`: asserts the sharding contract still holds (`ShardTests`: every name in exactly one shard for any count) and pins the one expected failure above, which the person's edit in Open questions resolves.
- No new tests are added: the hash-sharding property is already proven by `ShardTests`, and there is no behavior change to cover. No existing test is edited, deleted, or skipped by the builder.

## Done when

- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` holds `"server api" = 4` with the comment from step 2, and nothing else differs.
- [ ] `matrix.py matrix` lists exactly `server api 1/4` through `server api 4/4`.
- [ ] `test_ci_matrix` shows only the expected `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs` failure; all other tests pass.
- [ ] `git status` shows only `scripts/ci-shards.toml` modified.
- [ ] A person has applied the Open questions pin update, so `bot selftest` (a required check) is green before merge.
- [ ] The pull request's CI shows every `rust (test server api k/4)` shard under 5 minutes; if any is not, a person has applied the conditional split.

## Risks

- Hash skew: if a few of the ~1,200 tests dominate runtime, one shard could still run long, since a count cannot split a single test. Four shards of ~300 keep this unlikely; the conditional person-side split is the fallback.
- Compile dominates: each shard recompiles the group's binaries, so if compile alone nears 5 minutes no count helps. The estimate says otherwise, but only the pull request's CI proves it; the conditional split covers it.
- `bot selftest` stays red until the person updates the pin test (as happened after #3263, fixed by a person in #3280). The pull request must not merge before that edit.
- The issue lists only jobs over 7 minutes; another job sitting between 5 and 7 minutes is invisible to the bot and out of scope for this change.

## Open questions

- Person, required before merge: in `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`, replace `"cards", "server", "server api", "server practice", "server practice rulings", "ai", "ai slow",` with `"cards", "server", "server api 1/4", "server api 2/4", "server api 3/4", "server api 4/4", "server practice", "server practice rulings", "ai", "ai slow",`, and replace `self.assertEqual({(job["shard"], job["shards"]) for job in jobs.values()}, {(1, 1)})` with `self.assertEqual({(job["shard"], job["shards"]) for job in jobs.values()}, {(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4)})` (same style as #3280).
- Person, conditional: if any new shard still runs 5 minutes or more, replace the `server api` group in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` (lines 117-121) with two groups sharing its scope, cache, and `--config` flags, one with `test = "-p jackioh-server --lib --config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=1 -- api:: --skip api::practice::"` (`group = "server api lib"`) and one with `test = "-p jackioh-server --test server --config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=1 -- api:: --skip api::practice::"` (`group = "server api int"`), then read that pull request's shard logs to target any remaining slow subset.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````
